body: What is the quickest way to start a resume in Canva?
options: Search the templates for 'resume' and customise one
Draw every line by hand on a blank page
explanation: Templates give you a ready layout; you replace the text and adjust the colours.

body: Which download option is best for printing a poster you designed in Canva?
explanation: PDF Print gives a high-quality file meant for printing.

body: Which option moves a selected element in front of or behind other elements?
explanation: The Position menu controls layer order and alignment.

body: Which shortcut undoes your last action in Canva on Windows?
explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes; Ctrl + Y redoes.

body: Pink lines appear while you drag an element. What are they?
options: Alignment guides that help you line up elements
explanation: Guides appear when an element lines up with the page centre, edges or other elements.

body: How do you let a friend edit a design together with you?
options: Download it as a JPG and send it
Print it and hand it over
Use Share and give them access that allows editing
explanation: Sharing with edit access lets both of you work on the same design.

body: What do you add to put a heading on your design?
options: A text box (Text > Add a heading)
explanation: The Text panel has heading, subheading and body text styles.

body: How do you change the colour of some text?
options: Select the text and use the text colour button in the toolbar
explanation: The text colour button (shown as an 'A' with a colour bar) opens the colour picker.

body: Which shortcut groups selected elements so they move together?
explanation: Ctrl + G groups elements. Ctrl + B is bold text.

body: What is a frame used for in Canva?
options: Holding a photo inside a shape so the photo is cropped to that shape
explanation: Drag a photo onto a frame and it fills the shape, such as a circle for a profile photo.

body: Which approach gives a clean, professional resume?
options: Use a different font for each section
Fill every empty space with icons
Use one or two fonts, with consistent sizes for all headings
Use neon colours for the body text
explanation: Consistency makes a page look organised and easy to scan.

body: Your text is hard to read on top of a busy photo. What is the best fix?
options: Put a semi-transparent shape behind the text, or darken the photo
explanation: Raising the contrast between text and background makes it readable without losing the photo.

body: You need the same poster as an Instagram post and as an A4 print. What should you do?
options: Make a copy at the new size and rearrange the elements to fit
Stretch the Instagram design by dragging its corners
Take a screenshot and crop it
Print the Instagram version on A4
explanation: Different sizes need their own layout. Stretching or screenshots distort the design or lower the quality.

body: What does the Transparency setting do?
options: Makes an element see-through so what is behind it shows
explanation: Lower transparency values let the background show through.

body: What does locking an element do?
options: Stops it from being moved or edited by accident
explanation: Lock elements such as backgrounds so they stay put while you edit the rest.

body: What does 'visual hierarchy' mean in design?
options: Using the same size for all text
Making the most important information stand out first through size, weight and position
explanation: A clear hierarchy tells the reader what to look at first, second and third.

body: How do you show a Canva presentation full screen to an audience?
explanation: Present mode shows one page at a time, like a slide show.

body: Without paid features, how can you keep your brand colours exactly the same in every design?
options: Match the colours by eye each time
Screenshot old designs and trace them
Note the hex codes (for example #1E40AF) and type them into the colour picker
explanation: A hex code always gives exactly the same colour.

body: You want to use an image you found on Google in a design you will publish. What should you do?
options: Use it, because every image on Google is free
Use it, because credit is never needed
Use it only if you have the rights; otherwise use Canva's library or your own photos
Blur it slightly so it is allowed
explanation: Most images online are copyrighted. Search results do not give you permission to use them.

body: What is white space in a design?
options: A mistake that should be filled
Empty space around and between elements that makes the design easier to read
explanation: White space gives elements room and helps the reader focus.

body: Which font pairing is usually easy to read?
options: A bold sans-serif for headings with a simple sans-serif or serif for body text
An all-caps script font for body text
A comic-style font for a formal resume
explanation: Pair a strong heading font with a plain, readable body font.

body: Why line elements up to a grid or alignment guides?
options: Canva needs it before you can download
Aligned elements look organised and are easier to scan
explanation: Alignment creates visual order, so even simple designs look polished.

body: You are sending a multi-page brochure to a professional printer. Which download settings are best?
options: A JPG of the first page only
PDF Print with crop marks and bleed
explanation: Bleed extends the background past the trim line and crop marks show where to cut, so there are no white edges.

body: A logo looks sharp on screen but blurry when printed large. What is the most likely cause?
options: A low-resolution image was enlarged beyond its size
explanation: Enlarging a small raster image (PNG/JPG) spreads its pixels out. Use a higher-resolution or vector version.

body: Which text and background pair is most readable for people with low vision?
explanation: High contrast helps everyone. Red and green is also hard for people with colour blindness.

body: Your social media post looks fine on a laptop, but the text is unreadable in a phone feed. What is the best fix?
options: Use fewer words in larger text sized for a phone screen
explanation: Most people see posts on phones, often while scrolling. Design and preview at phone size.

body: You are designing a poster for a client. Which practice is copyright-safe?
options: Copy a Canva template and sell it as your own template
Use elements under Canva's licence terms or your own photos, and leave out logos you have no rights to
Add any popular song to the video
explanation: Licences have conditions, and trademarks and music have their own owners. Use only what you have rights to.

body: How do you keep a 10-page Canva presentation consistent?
options: Change the style on every page
Reuse the same layout, fonts and colours, for example by duplicating a styled page
Use different alignments on each page
explanation: Duplicating a finished page gives you a template that keeps every page in the same style.

body: For a calm, professional look, which colour approach works best?
options: One main colour plus neutrals, with a single accent colour
Only pure red and pure green
A rainbow gradient on all text
explanation: Limiting the palette keeps a design calm. The accent colour draws the eye to key items.

body: Your design has an animated element and is meant for Instagram. Which download format should you choose?
options: MP4 video (or GIF for a short loop)
explanation: Only video or GIF formats keep the animation. Image and PDF downloads are static.
